correctness.rationale: The drifted Gaussian resolvent and rank-one delta killing identity yield the exact free killing Laplace transform. Renewal gives m=(e^(a+u)(1+u/K)-1)/rho. The derivative numerator J=rho H'-H satisfies J'=rho H'', with H'' having exactly one negative-to-positive zero at most, while J is negative near zero and positive at infinity; exactly one global optimum follows. Uniform Taylor expansion near b=1 plus coercivity rigorously localizes optimal rates at K^(-1/3), deriving the unique cubic crossover root and mean excess, while fixed b>1 yields K^(-1/2). A standalone program passed 235 optimization/asymptotic assertions and 45 independent Gaussian-resolvent quadrature assertions. Finite tests do not substitute for the analytic all-parameter proofs.

value.rationale: The previously acknowledged drift-perfect-target switch is singular when the sink is only partially reactive. The exact finite-K optimum, its global uniqueness, distinct half- and third-power reactivity laws and explicit λ-dependent crossover answer a natural tuning problem for drift-biased reactive search, including sharp optimal cost corrections. This is not a tiny parameter gain, table recomputation or nomenclature substitution. Its relevance is limited to the specified delta-trap Poisson mechanism, and literature-wide priority remains best-knowledge.
